reason: E2 confirms laser cladding of TiC/Ni60 on Ti6Al4V and reports high hardness and improved tribological properties for TiC coatings on Ti alloys, directly supporting the feasibility and expected hardness increase. E1 supports the general mechanism that hard phases improve hardness and wear resistance, though it concerns a different coating system. The specific predicted 30–50% hardness increase and 50% wear reduction are not directly evidenced, and the mechanism of in situ TiC formation is not detailed in the cited passages.
premises: Laser cladding can deposit TiC-based composite coatings on Ti6Al4V alloy.
TiC coatings can achieve high surface microhardness (e.g., 1221.5 HV, 3.93× substrate).
TiC coatings improve tribological properties of titanium alloys.
Hard particles in a coating increase hardness and wear resistance by hindering dislocation motion.
